title: Budget and Revenue
text:
Film budgets and worldwide box office revenue. Figure 1 shows the relationship between them.

import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

films = pd.read_csv("films.csv")

plt.scatter(films["budget_musd"], films["revenue_musd"])
plt.xlabel("Budget (Million USD)")
plt.ylabel("Revenue (Million USD)")
plt.title("Budget vs. Revenue")
plt.show()







Figure 1: Film Budget vs. Worldwide Revenue

title: Runtime and Ratings
text:
The relationship between film runtime and IMDb ratings. Figure 1 shows how ratings vary with runtime.
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

films = pd.read_csv("films.csv")

plt.scatter(films["runtime_min"], films["imdb_rating"])
plt.xlabel("Runtime (Minutes)")
plt.ylabel("IMDb Rating")
plt.title("Runtime vs. Rating")
plt.show()







Figure 1: Film Runtime vs. IMDb Rating

title: The Bond Films
text:
The worldwide box office revenue of James Bond films over time.

import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

films = pd.read_csv("films.csv")
bond = films[films["franchise"] == "James Bond"]
bond = bond.sort_values("year")

The first Bond film in this dataset was released in 1995, and the last was released in 2021.

plt.plot(bond["year"], bond["revenue_musd"], marker="o")
plt.xlabel("Year")
plt.ylabel("Revenue (Million USD)")
plt.title("James Bond Box Office Revenue")
plt.show()
